posts.text:
BREAKING: HOLY SMOKES! Democrats now control enough states to effectively abolish the Electoral College through the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.

Republicans did NOT have this on their bingo cards...

Under the Constitution, states control their electoral votes and are allowed to decide how they are allocated during presidential elections. Currently, almost every state gives its votes to whoever wins the state.

In practice, the current system means that a candidate can win the national popular vote, but lose the election because small states like Wyoming exert undue influence on the outcome. That state has 3 electoral votes with a population of just 577,000 people. California has 54 electoral votes and a population of 39.5 million people. So a vote in Wyoming is essentially 3.8 times as valuable as one in California.

Since 1992, Democrats have won the popular vote seven out of nine times.

Under the NPV, states that join agree to give their electoral votes to whoever wins the national popular vote, not just their own state. So a state could go red on the map, but if the Democrat wins the national vote, they still get that state's votes. And vice versa of course.

The crucial mechanism is that the compact doesn't trigger until the member states have a combined power of at least 270 electoral votes, the number needed to win the White House. So far, 18 states plus D.C. have joined, totaling 222 electoral votes. We only need 48 more.

Now is the chance to pass this measure in every state possible. Democrats won both houses of the legislature in Wisconsin for the first time in 18 years (10 electoral votes). We won the Pennsylvania state Senate for the first time since 1993 (19 votes). We now have a trifecta in Michigan (15 votes). And we won the governor’s race in Nevada (6 votes).

10 + 19 + 15 + 6 = 50. 

222 + 50 = 272.

And if we hold our lead in the Arizona Senate, that number could climb as high as 283, more than enough to trigger the compact.

In addition to removing an imbalance in our system that favors Republicans, this novel approach would fundamentally change how candidates run their presidential campaigns. Currently, they are incentivized to ignore most of the country. If you live in a “safe” state, red or blue, your vote for President is basically decided before you cast it. Campaigns spend their time and money in a handful of swing states while the rest of us watch from the sidelines. If the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact is adopted, they'll have reason to hit every state because they're aiming to win the largest swath of the country as a whole, not just certain states.

States have until July 20, 2028 to join the compact in time for the next presidential election.

We can fix our democracy. The time is now.

Please like and share if you support this idea!

I’ve lost the ability to tell my family and friends “just wait, Trump will expose the fraud.” At this point I sound like the boy who cried wolf.

I remember 2017 and 2018. I told people any day now we would see the mass arrests. 

They never came. 

I remember 2020. This would be it. Trump would win and the justice phase would start. Biden took office. Arrests never came. 

I remember 2024. Same speech. Same certainty. And then the midterms. I was convinced we would see high-level arrests before last night. We didn’t.

So what do you do when you can’t say “just wait” anymore? 

You show the numbers. You keep pointing at the data as it comes out. 

Sixteen million early voting ballots cast. That is an outlier by any historical standard. 

Fourteen million of those would have had to break hard for Democrats to produce the margins we saw in the places that decided these races. 

I will keep posting the statistics and the inconsistencies as they surface over the next days and weeks. That is what I can actually do.

The rest is on President Trump, DHS, and DOJ. They either prosecute the fraud and arrest the people who ran it, or they don’t. 

I know it is frustrating. People will say I am moving the goalposts. Maybe. The honest answer is none of us know the exact timing. 

I still believe we will see the justice phase before the end of these next two years. I still believe nothing can stop what is coming. 

I do not know what that looks like between now and November 2028. I know what is at stake if it does not happen.

Yes, it feels like egg on the face as a digital soldier. Let them laugh. Let them mock. It is fine. I am not going to stop looking at the numbers or stop saying what I see. 

The alternative is accepting that the same machine keeps operating unchecked into 2028. I do not accept that. 

President Trump knows what is at stake. I still do too.

Over the years I have grown to greatly appreciate my digital soldier friends on X. In times like these I am thankful for the small chat groups of like-minded patriots who get it and who are living the same frustration. 

It reminds me of what the Continental soldiers must have felt in the dark days with General Washington. Everyone doubted them. Everyone mocked them. Everyone laughed. No one thought they had a chance. They held firm anyway because they believed in the dream that became the United States of America. 

In the same way, my friends and I will not stop. We know what the stakes are. I firmly believe nothing can stop what is coming.

posts.text:
Rest in peace, Bill Nunn. 🕊️

A beloved American actor, Bill Nunn left behind an unforgettable legacy through his memorable performances in film, television, and theater.

He was best known for portraying Radio Raheem in Spike Lee’s critically acclaimed film Do the Right Thing. His powerful performance, particularly the iconic “Love and Hate” speech, became one of the most memorable moments in the movie.

Beyond that role, Nunn was widely recognized for playing Joseph “Robbie” Robertson, the Daily Bugle editor, in Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man trilogy, starring alongside Tobey Maguire. He also appeared in popular films such as New Jack City, Sister Act, Regarding Henry, Mo’ Better Blues, He Got Game, The Legend of 1900, and Runaway Jury.

On television, he was known for playing Terrence “Pip” Phillips in The Job and Cash in the comedy series Sirens. He also appeared in Chicago Hope, The X-Files, and The District.

Throughout his career, Nunn became a respected character actor, particularly through his collaborations with filmmaker Spike Lee. He also supported young performers through the Bill Nunn Theatre Outreach Project, helping bring theater opportunities to students in Pittsburgh.

Born October 20, 1953, in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Bill Nunn passed away on September 24, 2016, at the age of 62, following a battle with leukemia.

Though he is gone, his unforgettable performances and the characters he brought to life will continue to entertain and inspire audiences for generations to come.

Thank you for the memorable performances, the iconic characters, and the lasting legacy you left behind, Bill Nunn.

Rest easy. You will never be forgotten. 🕊️
